design_rationale:
WORKLOG / TEST DOSSIER - task 1 of damage_claims_and_protection (category protect). Round 2 (rework after the policy-task audit).

1. WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST. A Nashville business host asks to accept the settlement on his approved lost-bookings claim. The number depends on two claims he never mentions: the income-loss rule's two prerequisite sentences say its settlement is not fixed until the stay's approved property-damage and pet-damage claims carry their reimbursements, because the stay bears one deductible and the income-loss claim bears only what the reimbursed claims have not. The agent settles both damage claims first (five factors each) and then the lost income (five factors, two read from the listing's calendar and the host's cancellation records).

2. SCOPE SNAPSHOT. Draw (scripts/draw_counts.py --task 1): key env_0045_vacation_rental_platform/damage_claims_and_protection/1, prerequisite_problems=2, factor_counts=[5, 5, 5]. Occupied by task 0: theft and valuables. Claimed here: protect_ext_property_settlement (pay_property_damage_reimbursement_941cbbf5, agent), protect_ext_pet_damage_settlement (pay_pet_damage_reimbursement_a5391300, agent), protect_ext_income_loss_settlement (accept_income_loss_settlement_ab094655, user). Every extended policy is now claimed once. Same declared deviation as task 0 (payout trigger on reimbursement rows; no payout write).

3. POLICIES, LINEAGE, TRIGGERS. All three refine protect_evt_reimbursement and list protect_agg_plan_year_limits. Property and pet: state_due. Income loss: on_request. Declared overwrites: the order clause (shares give the adjusted loss), the guest-payment clause (recovery-sharing method), 'subtract deductible_usd' (per-stay share / unborne remainder), and for income loss the nightly-subtotal clause (lost-nights proration).

4. PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root: protect_ext_income_loss_settlement. Prerequisites: protect_ext_property_settlement and protect_ext_pet_damage_settlement (fan-out). Edge income -> property: value_input, gate in_stay_settled, form state, sentence 'The income-loss settlement is not fixed until the plan's HostCover ledger shows a reimbursement on every approved property-damage claim of the same stay.' Edge income -> pet: value_input, gate in_stay_settled, form state, sentence 'The income-loss settlement is likewise not fixed until the ledger shows a reimbursement on every approved pet-damage claim of the same stay.' Four-point test, both: (1) ordering connective 'not ... until', negated direction, the way a desk states a figure that waits on other bookings ('not fixed until'); rewritten affirmatively it is 'fixed only after the ledger shows a reimbursement on every approved ... claim of the same stay', nothing added or dropped (task 0's sentence runs in the affirmative direction, so the charter carries both). (2) The waited-on side is a record-visible state: reimbursement entries on the stay's approved claims of the named category in the HostCover ledger. (3) No tool, policy id or code token ('property-damage', 'pet-damage' are hyphenated words). (4) Scope exact: every approved claim of that category on the same stay (closed set named by category), matching each edge's condition. One write per state: only pay_property_damage_reimbursement_941cbbf5 books a reimbursement on a property-damage claim and only pay_pet_damage_reimbursement_a5391300 on a pet-damage claim; each rule says its figure is the reimbursement Roamhaven books on that claim. Derivation: sentence + records (claims 605bc43f-bf0a-4bef-8233-b091275533b3 and a85b2e37-7dfa-49f4-a3b4-4c0c027fba33 approved, their only ledger rows a request and a partial guest payment) + the damage rules -> settle each with its tool. False at the opening: no protect_reimbursement_paid row exists on the plan. The customer's own act is the root accept_income_loss_settlement_ab094655 (lost-income settlements rest on his own cancelled booking; he confirms and accepts at hand-over). Topological order: property, pet (either order), income. Deletion sensitivity (actual run): skipping either damage write -> income 567.48 instead of 648.59. user_scenario never names a damage claim; tools validate nothing.

5. BASE-INVARIANT CARD. claim_approved: claim_status approved on all three claims (decided 2026-10-01). escalated_in_time (anchor guest_response_due_at, not_after, escalation_window_days 30, calendar days from the deadline's date part, inclusive): property and pet deadline 2026-08-23, escalated 2026-09-04 (day 12; last standing day 2026-09-22, day 31 = 2026-09-23 fails); income deadline 2026-08-27, escalated 2026-09-21 (day 25; last day 2026-09-26). one_reimbursement_per_claim: no reimbursement row on any of the three. protect_agg_plan_year_limits: policy_scope; nothing paid since the 2026-03-15 plan-year start. Coverage: the stay checked in 2026-08-14 under Plus (changed 2026-02-16), plan active; Plus covers income loss (income_loss_covered true, 7 nights).

6. BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Damaged stay 4006f145-bb4d-44d0-b1d0-83cc8477f0eb (Kelsey Brandt ee31fdee-b5c2-4c14-ad95-ec79f526f4c4, 2026-08-14 to 2026-08-18, one dog) under plan d49a983f-77a5-4c2d-851b-c6f719303800 on listing 9fadc62c-0ffb-478e-90b2-3d0899d52cc2. Claims keyed by claim_id: property 605bc43f-bf0a-4bef-8233-b091275533b3, pet a85b2e37-7dfa-49f4-a3b4-4c0c027fba33, income 4634294e-1189-403c-9f68-346b4ba692f1. Guest payments 60.00 / 35.00 / 20.00 each on its own claim. The cancelled booking 1f113763-69c9-4622-89d8-31411ab77895 (Ramon Delgado 6af5e898-1261-4e77-9453-27e2abbfbc26, 2026-08-21 to 2026-08-30, cancelled_by_host 2026-08-19) is the lost income: its calendar block (listing record) and host cancellation (host record, initiated by host, band 30_days_to_48_hours, penalty 502.50 charged) are read through stay_id. Excluded: the premium and the requests (not guest payments); each claim's payment only on its own claim. Nothing settled yet.

7. FACTOR CARD (actual run). Property (expected 1499.07; all-baseline 2456.67): depreciation 30 months -> 20 percent (baseline 1918.07); condition: most recent quality review (2026-10-01, whose 365-day rating window covers the stay) warning -> 85 percent (cross listing; near-miss the 2026-04-01 pass; baseline 1794.80); escalation 12 days -> 95 percent (baseline 1587.24); deductible factor Professional Host AND Entire Home -> 1.5 (multi-source, cross host; baseline 1539.24); recovery-sharing HostCover Plus -> proportional (baseline insurer-first 1494.60). Pet (expected 555.49; all-baseline 1331.67): depreciation 48 months -> 40 percent (baseline 1000.06); pet-fee share, listing pet fee 75.00 -> 90 percent (cross listing; the pet fee the guest paid covers part of a pet's impact, as the cleaning fee offsets a deep-cleaning claim in base; baseline 629.44); condition warning -> 90 percent (baseline 629.44); escalation 12 days -> 95 percent (baseline 590.51); recovery-sharing proportional (baseline 551.13). Income (expected 648.59; all-baseline 1786.67): lost-nights 9 blocked > 7 -> x 7/9 (cross listing; baseline 862.30); cancellation timing host-initiated AND 30_days_to_48_hours -> 80 percent (multi-source, cross host; baseline 835.57); escalation 25 days -> 85 percent (baseline 780.56); new-cover 179 days -> 75 percent (cross host; baseline 897.93); recovery-sharing proportional (baseline 646.37).

8. THE RECOVERY-SHARING METHOD (replaces the round-1 guest-payment ladder). Property-claim practice allocates money recovered from the responsible party by one of three rules: the insured made whole first, proportional sharing, or the insurer credited first. The tier follows the HostCover level: Premier, Elite and Estate make the host whole first (only the larger of guest payments and deductible is subtracted); Standard and Plus share proportionally (the deductible plus the guest payments times the adjusted loss less the deductible, divided by the adjusted loss); Essential credits Roamhaven first (both subtracted, the baseline). With a guest payment standing the three give different figures (property here: 1499.07 proportional, 1554.60 made whole first, 1494.60 insurer first).

9. PERSONA DESIGN. Darnell is brisk and businesslike, a business owner who wants the matter closed. He volunteers his name and the lost-bookings settlement he wants to accept; gives phone 6155275318 and licence last four 5642 when asked; identifies the claim by the August 14 to 18 stay and the Delgado booking he cancelled on August 19. He knows no reference numbers, mentions the dog and table damage only if asked, agrees to whatever must be paid first without details, questions once why the figure is below the 1,890 booking and accepts the answer, runs the acceptance with exactly the agent's values, keeps his business account, and closes when told the settlement is booked.

10. STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate, verify, read plan, claims, ledger, stays (by host account and by each guest), listing and its records, host account and its records, payout methods. The income-loss rule's prerequisite sentences -> both damage claims unreimbursed -> property 2600.00 x 0.80 x 0.85 x 0.95 = 1679.60, deductible 250/3 x 1.5 = 125.00, proportional offset 125.00 + 60.00 x 1554.60 / 1679.60 = 180.53 -> 1499.07 (pay_property_damage_reimbursement_941cbbf5); pet 1450.00 x 0.60 x 0.90 x 0.90 x 0.95 = 669.465, deductible 83.33, offset 83.33 + 35.00 x 586.13 / 669.465 = 113.98 -> 555.49 (pay_pet_damage_reimbursement_a5391300); then income 1890.00 x 7/9 x 0.80 x 0.85 x 0.75 = 749.70, deductible 250 x 1/3 = 83.33, offset 83.33 + 20.00 x 666.37 / 749.70 = 101.11 -> 648.59, handed to Darnell with accept_income_loss_settlement_ab094655.

11. VERIFICATION. A temporary authoring script (removed at the end of the run) replayed the gold writes with check_compute's evaluator: property 1499.07 (1918.07 / 1794.80 / 1587.24 / 1539.24 / 1494.60, all 2456.67); pet 555.49 (1000.06 / 629.44 / 629.44 / 590.51 / 551.13, all 1331.67); income 648.59 (862.30 / 835.57 / 780.56 / 897.93 / 646.37, all 1786.67); edges: either damage write skipped -> 567.48, both -> 486.37. Writing pet before property gives the same terminal hash and figures. No declared figure sits on a half-cent tie.

12. CLOSURE. property -> pay_property_damage_reimbursement_941cbbf5 -> computations[0] (step 14, 1499.07); pet -> pay_pet_damage_reimbursement_a5391300 -> computations[1] (step 16, 555.49); income -> accept_income_loss_settlement_ab094655 -> computations[2] (step 18, 648.59). charter_scope = required_documents in resolution order. No handoff, no extra write.

13. SOLVABILITY AGAINST GT. Every call cites the approved claim row (claim_status, claim_id), the deadline and escalation fields with frozen_time, and the claim's request row for the once-per-claim dedup; bindings tie claim_id to the tool argument. Stage facts pre-exist in initial_state.

14. DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT. From the three rules, schemas, finder returns and persona alone: same objects, the damage writes in either order then the income acceptance, same amounts.

15. REVISIONS. Round 2 (audit items): F-G1 - the guest-payment ladder in property, pet and income had two distinct outcomes; replaced by the recovery-sharing method (made whole first / proportional / Roamhaven first, keyed to the HostCover level). O-L3 - the condition-share rule now states that a quality review rates the year before it, so the 2026-10-01 review reflects the condition around the August stay. O-L4 - the pet-fee share is grounded in the pet fee the guest paid (offset logic of base's deep-cleaning rule) instead of 'ordinary wear'. Rounding now 'half up' in every rule. Figures moved: property 1554.60 -> 1499.07, pet 586.13 -> 555.49, income 666.37 -> 648.59.
user_scenario:
You are Darnell Okoro, owner of Okoro Stays LLC in Nashville. Your business rents out a three-bedroom house on Roamhaven called Music Row Bungalow with Fenced Yard. You are brisk and businesslike, a little tired of this whole episode, and you want it wrapped up today.

In August a group stayed at the bungalow from the 14th to the 18th with their dog and left the place torn up. The house was not fit for the next guests, so you had to cancel the Delgado family's nine-night booking that was starting on August 21. You claimed the lost bookings on your HostCover plan, and this week you were told the claims team approved your lost-bookings claim and that you have to confirm the cancelled booking and accept the lost-income settlement yourself. That is why you are calling: you want to accept the lost-income settlement and get the money paid out. You have not seen a figure.

You start by giving your name and saying you are calling about the lost-bookings claim. When the agent asks how to find you, you give your mobile number, 6155275318. When the agent needs to confirm who you are, you give the last four of your driver's license, 5642; if asked for more, your email is darnell@okorostays.com and your date of birth is September 3, 1977. You do not have any claim or plan numbers handy; if asked which claim, you say it is the one for the bookings you lost after the August 14 to 18 stay, the Delgado booking you cancelled on August 19. If the agent asks what else the dog and the guests damaged, you say the dog chewed up doors and scratched the floors and the guests broke the glass dining table, and that you filed for those too.

If the agent says other claims from that stay have to be paid before the lost-income settlement can be offered, you say fine, go ahead and do it; you do not ask for the details. When the agent gives you the settlement figure, you point out that the Delgado booking was worth 1,890 dollars and ask how they got to a lower number; you accept whatever the agent explains and never put forward a figure of your own. When the agent hands you the step to confirm and accept the settlement yourself, you use exactly the claim reference and amount the agent gives you and you read back the confirmation. The money should go to the business bank account already on file, and you do not want to change your payout setup or your plan. Once the agent confirms the settlement is accepted and booked, you say thanks and end the call.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The two damage settlements are parallel prerequisites of the income-loss settlement. Neither reads the other's write: each divides the deductible by the stay's approved claims (3), not by its reimbursed ones, and no other input touches the reimbursements. Actual run (temporary authoring replay, removed after the run; repeated in round 2): writing the pet reimbursement before the property reimbursement gives the same terminal DB hash and the same values 1499.07, 555.49 and 648.59. The income-loss settlement comes after both, as its two prerequisite sentences state.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping step 14: the stay counts 1 reimbursed claim of 3, the income-loss claim bears 166.67 and the settlement recomputes to 567.48 instead of 648.59; the property reimbursement row is also missing.
Skipping step 16: likewise 1 of 3 reimbursed, deductible 166.67, settlement 567.48 instead of 648.59; the pet-damage reimbursement row is also missing.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario asks only to accept the lost-income settlement. It never names the property-damage or pet-damage claim, their reimbursements or any earlier step; the dog and table damage come up only if the agent asks what else was damaged, and the one conditional about 'other claims from that stay' fires only after the agent says so, with the customer agreeing without asking for details.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: task_tools.py pay_property_damage_reimbursement_941cbbf5, pay_pet_damage_reimbursement_a5391300 and accept_income_loss_settlement_ab094655 each look up the claim only to copy its plan, host, stay and verified loss onto the new ledger row and then call ctx.create unconditionally; none checks approval, escalation, other claims of the stay or earlier reimbursements, and none returns an error. Calling the income-loss acceptance first writes its row just the same, with whatever amount is passed.
